app.envThe settings and, above all, APP_SECRET. Without it, the encrypted credentials in a database backup cannot be read.
*.local.php filesYour own plans, credit rates and tool servers.
haraka/configIf you receive mail: its configuration and DKIM keys.
 
mongodump --uri="$MONGO_URI" --db="$MONGO_DB" --archive=netflow9-$(date +%F).gz --gzip

Keep backups off the server, and keep app.env separate from database backups: together they give access to every stored secret.

Restoring

  1. Install the same NetFlow9 version and put back app.env and your *.local.php files.
  2. Restore the database: mongorestore --uri=… --archive=… --gzip.
  3. Run ./v seed::indexes, then start PHP-FPM and the services.

Upgrading

  1. Back up, as above.
  2. Stop the daemon: sudo systemctl stop nfn-daemon.
  3. Replace the application files with the new version. Keep app.env, *.local.php, logs/, var/, run/ and haraka/. From git: git pull, then git submodule update --init, which brings the libraries in app/pkgs to the versions the new version uses.
  4. Create any new indexes: ./v seed::indexes.
  5. Restart PHP-FPM and the daemon: sudo systemctl restart php-fpm nfn-daemon.
  6. Run the check suite: app/commands/CheckCommand.sh.

Warning: do not use git submodule update --remote. It moves each library to the newest code of its own repository instead of the version NetFlow9 was tested with.

pages.title: Security
pages.summary: Hardening a NetFlow9 installation: secrets, database access, HTTPS, sign-in protection and the audit log.
pages.html:
Secrets

  • Credentials and other secret fields are encrypted with APP_SECRET (app.env). Keep app.env readable by the app's user only, and back it up separately.
  • Secret fields are write-only in the app: after saving, they are never shown again, and they are masked in the audit log.
  • Workflows refer to credentials by name, so exporting or sharing a workflow exposes no secret.

MongoDB access

Turn on MongoDB authorization with separate users. The installer does it when you choose Secure MongoDB (offered while MongoDB is on the same machine and does not require sign-in yet). Alone, sudo scripts/3_mongo-auth-setup.sh, run as root while authorization is still off, creates:

  • nfn_admin (root), for operators. Its connection string is written to a file readable only by root: move it to a password manager, then delete the file.
  • nfn_app (read and write on the app's database), written into app.env.
  • nfn_haraka (only what inbound mail needs), written into app.env (HARAKA_MONGO_URI) and, when Haraka is installed, into its configuration.

The passwords are random and never printed. Then enable authorization in mongod.conf and restart MongoDB (the installer does both, and restarts the services).

Web

  • Serve only HTTPS, with HSTS (see nginx and PHP-FPM).
  • Pages carry a Content-Security-Policy (scripts, styles, images and connections from the site only), X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN and a restrictive Permissions-Policy.
  • Uploaded files are downloaded as attachments, never run in the app's origin. Only images are shown inline.
  • Keep APP_DEBUG=false. Errors then show only a reference, and the details go to logs/app.log.

Sign-in

  • Failed sign-ins and password reset requests are rate-limited per address and per email.
  • Owners can enforce two-factor authentication and set session limits per account. Super-admins always need 2FA.
  • A password reset ends the user's other sessions.

Outgoing requests

  • HTTP Request and Download File may call only public addresses unless HTTP_STEPS_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true. Each redirect is checked again.
  • The web browser tool server runs as its own user and is blocked from private networks by a firewall table.
  • Expressions and Code steps run in a sandbox (J): they can only read the run's variables, with time and step limits.

Audit log

Audit entries are sealed. ./v audit::verify reports entries that were changed, forged or removed. Audit entries are kept at least one year.

pages.title: Architecture
pages.summary: How NetFlow9 is built: the PHP application, MongoDB, the daemon, plugins and the browser code.
pages.html:
NetFlow9 is a PHP application on its own small framework (V), with MongoDB as its database and plain JavaScript in the browser, styled with Bootstrap 5.

Parts

PartWhereWhat
Frameworkapp/sys/The V framework: routing, controllers, views, models (BaseModel), fields, sessions, hooks, the J language (sys/J).
Controllers, viewsapp/controllers/, app/views/<controller>/Pages and JSON endpoints, at /<controller>/<action>.
Modelsapp/models/Accounts, users, projects, workflows, executions, credentials, files, data tables. Each declares its schema: fields, types, permissions, rules.
Stepsapp/models/node/One class per step type (NodeApp*, NodeCore*, NodeTrigger*).
Utilitiesapp/util/Expressions, HTTP, email, formats, conditions, tiers…
Librariesapp/pkgs/Third-party PHP libraries, as git submodules pinned to a release or commit: the MongoDB PHP library, ReactPHP (event-loop, stream, child-process), evenement, php-qrcode, php-asn1. Each is loaded through autoload in app/config.php. php-qrcode's settings container is util\SettingsContainer (in place of chillerlan/php-settings-container).
Pluginsapp/plugins/<Name>/Optional features with their own models, controllers, views and commands, enabled in app/plugins.php.
Consoleapp/commands/, app/vCommands (./v <command>::<action>), including the daemon and the check suite.
Browserpublic_html/js/app.js (sidebar, theme, formatters), app.workflow.js (the designer), app.pjax.js (page loads without full reloads), forms, grids, editors.
Themepublic_html/css/theme.cssBootstrap 5.3.8 with NetFlow9's styles, built from SCSS.

How a workflow runs

  1. A trigger creates an execution (WfExecution): a copy of the version's steps and connections, with a token on the trigger.
  2. The execution moves tokens along connections. Each step's execute() returns the outputs to continue on, SLEEP to wait, or nothing (Merge waiting for its other inputs).
  3. Runs started by people (Run, forms, tasks) may run inside the web request. One still running after SYNC_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT seconds (default 30) is handed to the daemon, which continues it from where it got to. Others are queued as jobs and run by the daemon's workers.
  4. A sleeping execution (Wait, human task) is saved with its wake-up time. The daemon resumes it then.

Multi-tenancy

Every record belongs to an account (aid). Models check access through the user's role and its scopes: global, project or own. Project-scoped records also require membership in their project.

pages.title: Calling webhooks
pages.summary: Starting workflows from your own code: requests, authentication and signatures, answers and retries.
pages.html:
A Webhook trigger lets any system start a workflow with an HTTP request. This page is about calling it from your code.

The request

  • Address: https://<your NetFlow9>/hook/<token>, shown in the trigger's settings.
  • Method: the one set in the trigger (POST by default, or Any).
  • Body: JSON, a web form or text, as set in Content type. At most 1 MB.
  • The workflow must be published. Requests to a draft are refused.

In the workflow, the request is the webhook variable: webhook.body (decoded JSON or form), webhook.query, webhook.headers (lower-case names), webhook.method, webhook.raw, webhook.ip.

Examples

# curl
curl -X POST "https://netflow.example.com/hook/3f9c…e1" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WEBHOOK_SECRET" \
  -d '{"order": 1042, "email": "ana@example.com"}'
// JavaScript (Node.js 18+ or a browser backend)
const res = await fetch('https://netflow.example.com/hook/3f9c…e1', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + process.env.WEBHOOK_SECRET },
  body: JSON.stringify({ order: 1042, email: 'ana@example.com' }),
});
console.log(res.status, await res.json());   // 202 { execution, state: "accepted" }
# Python
import os, requests
r = requests.post("https://netflow.example.com/hook/3f9c…e1",
                  json={"order": 1042, "email": "ana@example.com"},
                  headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["WEBHOOK_SECRET"]})
print(r.status_code, r.json())

Signing requests (HMAC)

With Authentication = HMAC-SHA256 signature of the body, send the HMAC-SHA256 of the exact body bytes, keyed with the secret, in the header you named. The value is hex, or sha256=<hex>.

# Python
import hmac, hashlib, json, requests
body = json.dumps({"order": 1042}).encode()
sig = hmac.new(SECRET.encode(), body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
requests.post(URL, data=body, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", "X-Signature": "sha256=" + sig})
// Node.js
const crypto = require('crypto');
const body = JSON.stringify({ order: 1042 });
const sig = crypto.createHmac('sha256', SECRET).update(body).digest('hex');
await fetch(URL, { method: 'POST', body, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'X-Signature': 'sha256=' + sig } });

Answers

StatusMeaning
202Accepted, with {"execution": "<id>", "state": "accepted"}. The workflow runs afterwards. This is the default.
200With Respond: When the workflow ends: the run finished, with {"execution": "<id>", "state": "end" | "error" | "sleep"}.
400The body is not valid JSON (content type JSON).
401Authentication failed.
404No such webhook.
405, 415Wrong method, or wrong content type.
409The workflow is not published, or has errors and cannot run.
413Body too large.
429Too many runs answering at once for this account. Retry after the Retry-After seconds.

Refused requests are recorded in the account's execution log, which helps when setting up a caller.

Tip: keep the webhook fast for the caller. Use When received, and let the workflow do the slow work. When the caller needs a result later, have the workflow call back, or write the result where the caller can read it.

pages.title: The MCP server
pages.summary: Letting AI assistants (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, others) work with a project through the Model Context Protocol.
pages.html:
Each project can be reached by AI assistants through NetFlow9's MCP server (Model Context Protocol), for example Claude Desktop or Claude Code. With a token, the assistant can query and change data tables, read files, list and run workflows, and build workflows, within the permissions of the user who made the token. The MCP server is part of NetFlow9 itself, on every plan.

Tokens

Tokens are made per project, on the MCP server tokens page at /token/list. The link is not in the menu yet.

  1. Create a token and give it a name that says what uses it, such as Claude Desktop.
  2. Copy it at once: it is shown only once. The page also shows the server URL and a ready client configuration.

A token acts as the user who made it, on the token's project, with that user's permissions. Delete it to revoke it. The list shows when each token was last used.

Connecting a client

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "netflow9": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://netflow.example.com/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <token>" }
    }
  }
}

This works, for example, as Claude Code's .mcp.json. The server speaks the Streamable HTTP transport with JSON answers, without streams or sessions, and supports the protocol versions 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05.

Tools

ToolDoes
list_tablesThe project's data tables and their columns.
query_tableRows matching conditions, sorted and paged.
insert_rowsAdds up to 100 rows. All are checked first: nothing is inserted if one fails.
update_row, delete_rowChanges or deletes one row.
create_table, update_tableCreates a table with its columns, or renames one.
add_column, update_column, delete_columnManages columns. Key, type and target cannot be changed.
list_workflowsThe workflows, their status and trigger, and whether they can be run.
run_workflowRuns a workflow with a Manual trigger and waits: its published version, else its draft. Returns the state, error and variables. queued: it ran too long for the request, the daemon finishes it (see get_execution).
get_executionAn execution's state, error, times, variables and last 50 log lines.
list_files, read_file, read_imageThe project's files, a text file (256 KB at most) or the text of a PDF or Office document (20 MB at most), an image (5 MB at most).
list_step_typesThe step types with their settings, outputs and variables, to build workflows.
get_workflow, create_workflow, update_workflowReads, creates or replaces a workflow's draft as steps and connections. Drafts are never published by the assistant: a person publishes them.
list_variablesThe project variables.

The same tools are offered to the AI steps (Use these tools) and power the designer's Assistant.

Security

  • Every call is checked against the token user's permissions, in the token's project only.
  • Requests from web pages of other sites are refused (protection against DNS rebinding).
  • Request bodies are limited to 1 MB.

pages.title: The expression language (J)
pages.summary: Reference of J, the safe JavaScript subset used by expressions and the Code step.
pages.html:
Expressions ({{ … }}) and the Code step use J, a sandboxed subset of JavaScript. If you know JavaScript, you know J: the differences are listed below.

Supported

  • var, let, const. Functions, arrow functions, default and rest parameters, closures.
  • if, for, for…of, for…in, while, do…while, switch, break, continue, return, throw, try / catch / finally.
  • All operators, including **, ??, ??=, &&=, ||=, ?., typeof, in, delete.
  • Template literals, array and object literals with spread, shorthand, computed keys and methods.
  • Built-ins: Math, JSON, Date, RegExp, Object.keys / values / entries / assign / fromEntries, Array.isArray / from / of, String, Number, Boolean, parseInt, parseFloat, isNaN, isFinite, Error, console.log (Code step).

Not supported

class, new, this, super, import / export, async / await, generators, with, getters and setters, instanceof, destructuring, labels and tagged templates. These are reported as errors in the editor.

Methods

ValuesMethods
Stringsat, charAt, charCodeAt, codePointAt, concat, endsWith, includes, indexOf, lastIndexOf, localeCompare, match, matchAll, padEnd, padStart, repeat, replace, replaceAll, search, slice, split, startsWith, substring, toLowerCase, toUpperCase, trim, trimEnd, trimStart
Arraysat, concat, every, fill, filter, find, findIndex, findLast, findLastIndex, flat, flatMap, forEach, includes, indexOf, join, lastIndexOf, map, pop, push, reduce, reduceRight, reverse, shift, slice, some, sort, splice, unshift
NumberstoFixed, toString
Datesget… / set… (FullYear, Month, Date, Hours, Minutes, Seconds, Milliseconds, with UTC variants), getDay, getTime, getTimezoneOffset, toISOString, toDateString, toTimeString, toUTCString, toLocaleString…
Regular expressionsexec, test

NetFlow9's functions

FunctionGives
markdown(text)Markdown as safe HTML. In an email, {{ markdown(…) }} alone in its braces shows it formatted.

Dates

  • Call Date without new: Date() is now, Date("2026-10-20T10:00"), Date(2026, 9, 20) (months 0–11), Date.now(), Date.parse(text).
  • Local time is the installation's time zone.
  • Accepted text: ISO 8601 (a date alone is UTC midnight, a date and time without an offset is local time) and the usual forms like Oct 20 2026 10:00. Relative text like tomorrow gives an Invalid Date.
  • b - a is the difference in milliseconds. < and > compare.
  • Dates leave an expression as ISO 8601 text.

Regular expressions

Literals (/(\d+)-(\d+)/g) and RegExp(pattern, flags), with the flags d g i m s u y. The string methods match, matchAll (an array), search, replace / replaceAll (with $1, $<name>, or a function) and split work as in JavaScript. Matching is on Unicode characters. A pattern that backtracks too much stops the run.

Differences from JavaScript

  • String length and positions count Unicode characters: "😀".length is 1.
  • Objects have no prototypes. Functions have no call, apply or bind.
  • Object keys keep their insertion order.
  • JSON.parse is tolerant: comments, single quotes, unquoted keys and trailing commas are accepted.
  • toLocale… methods always format like en-US.

Sandbox and limits

  • A script sees only the built-ins and the run's variables. It can't reach files, the network or the server.
  • The run's variables are copies: in an expression, changing them changes nothing. In the Code step, assigning a top-level name sets that workflow variable.
  • An expression may run for one second and a limited number of operations. A Code step runs up to its timeout (at most 30 seconds). Reaching a limit stops the run, and try / catch cannot catch it.

pages.title: Plugins and hooks
pages.summary: How plugins extend NetFlow9: their structure, registering models and steps, and the hooks they can use.
pages.html:
Optional features are plugins: LDAP, SAML, inbound mail, the System AI, the administration, and more. A plugin is a folder in app/plugins/, listed in app/plugins.php to enable it.

Structure

app/plugins/Example/
  Plugin.php          class plugins\Example\Plugin: registers everything in its constructor
  models/             its models, steps (Node*) and credentials (Credential*)
  controllers/        its pages: /Example/<controller>/<action>
  views/              their views
  commands/           its console commands: ./v Example::<command>::<action>
  util/               its helpers

Classes are in the plugin's namespace (plugins\Example\models\…) and load automatically.

A plugin's constructor

namespace plugins\Example;

class Plugin {
    public function __construct() {
        // its models: a step, a credential kind (a variant of Credential), a model
        \V::app()->om->registerObjects([
            'NodeAppExample' => [ 'class' => __NAMESPACE__ . '\\models\\NodeAppExample', 'wfNode' => true ],
            'CredentialExample' => [ 'class' => __NAMESPACE__ . '\\models\\CredentialExample', 'variant-of' => 'Credential' ],
        ]);

        // hooks, in every mode (web and console: the daemon runs the steps)
        \V::app()->hooks->addHook('execution:end', [ models\NodeAppExample::class, 'afterExecutionEnd' ]);

        if (\V::app()->config('app.mode') != 'web')
            return;

        // web only: a link in the Settings menu
        \V::app()->hooks->addHook('layout:settings-menu', function() {
            if (\V::app()->user->can('Account::update'))
                echo '<a href="/Example/example/settings" class="nav-link"><i class="bi bi-gear"></i> Example</a>';
        });
    }
}

A registry entry may also name a feature (e.g. 'feature' => 'google'). The step or credential is then available only to accounts whose plan has that feature. Declare the feature with the tiers:features hook.

Hooks

Add a hook with \V::app()->hooks->addHook($name, $callable, $priority = 10). Lower priorities run first.

HookCalled
on:init, on:start, on:before-router, on:after-router, on:before-action, on:after-action, on:endThe request's life cycle.
on:after-user-loginAfter a user signs in.
identity:authenticate, identity:password-sourceSign-in with another source (LDAP, SAML): check a password, or say that a user's password is kept elsewhere.
site:login-linksLinks on the sign-in page (e.g. Sign in with SSO).
model:after-save, model:after-deleteAfter any model is saved or deleted, with the values before. The audit log uses them.
workflow:before-save, workflow:after-save, workflow:before-deleteAround saving and deleting workflows.
execution:endWhen an execution ends.
daemon:tickRegularly, in the daemon.
layout:settings-menu, layout:aside-project-menu, layout:page-topEcho links or notices into the menus and pages.
workflow:designer-toolbar, workflow:designer-panelsButtons and panels in the designer.
mcp:tools, ai:mcp-servers, ai:system-providerTools offered to the AI steps and the Assistant (besides NetFlow9's own MCP server tools), MCP servers offered to the AI steps, and the System AI.
tiers:features, tiers:usage, tiers:changedPlan features, usage figures, and plan changes.
admin:services, admin:installation-panels, admin:account-panels, admin:account-features, admin:account-summaryServices and sections in the administration pages.

Hooks that collect something pass an \ArrayObject for the handler to fill. For example, tiers:features gets $features, and the handler adds $features['ldap'] = 'LDAP sign-in'.

Permissions

A plugin can add permissions for its models (for example McpToken::create) with data\SysPermissions::register() in its constructor. They then appear in the role editor.

pages.title: Writing a step
pages.summary: Adding a step type: its class, settings schema, variables, outputs and execution.
pages.html:
A step type is a PHP class extending \models\WfNode, registered with 'wfNode' => true. In the core, steps live in app/models/node/. In a plugin, they live in its models/ and are registered in its constructor (see Plugins and hooks).

A complete example

namespace plugins\Example\models;

class NodeAppGreeting extends \models\WfNode {
    public static $type = 'app';                  // trigger | core | app
    public static $name = 'greeting';             // the type is app::greeting
    public static $label = 'Greeting';
    public static $icon = 'bi-chat-heart';
    public static $color = 'var(--wf-color-app)';
    public static $inputs = 1;
    public static $outputs = 1;

    // the settings, shown in the step's dialog and checked when saving
    public static function configSchema() {
        return [
            [ 'key' => 'variable', 'type' => 'text', 'label' => 'Result variable', 'required' => true, 'default' => 'greeting',
              'ui' => [ 'variableName' => 'write', 'width' => 3 ] ],
            [ 'key' => 'name', 'type' => 'text', 'label' => 'Name', 'required' => true,
              'help' => 'Who to greet, e.g. {{ form_user.name }}', 'ui' => [ 'expression' => true ] ],
            [ 'key' => 'style', 'type' => 'select', 'label' => 'Style', 'default' => 'warm',
              'choices' => [ 'warm' => 'Warm', 'formal' => 'Formal' ] ],
        ];
    }

    // the variables it sets: the designer suggests them in later steps
    public static function outputVariables($config) {
        $name = (string)($config['variable'] ?? 'greeting');
        return \util\Validator::isIdentifier($name) ? [ $name => [ 'type' => 'string', 'info' => 'the greeting' ] ] : [];
    }

    // the work: returns the outputs to continue on
    public function execute($edgeId = null) {
        $who = (string)$this->expr('name', '');              // {{ }} evaluated
        $text = $this->cfg('style') === 'formal' ? "Good day, {$who}." : "Hi {$who}!";
        $this->exec->setVariable((string)$this->cfg('variable', 'greeting'), $text);
        $this->exec->log($this->wfid, 'greeted ' . $who);
        return [ 0 ];
    }
}

Settings schema

Each setting is a field: key, type (text, textarea, number, select, switch, checkbox, nested for rows…), label, help, default, required, choices, and validate rules. The ui options shape the dialog:

  • expression: the field takes {{ }}, with suggestions and checks (true, or 'reference' for a variable only).
  • variableName: 'write': the field names a variable the step sets, shown on the canvas.
  • width (of 12), newRow, placeholder, rows.
  • showIf / hideIf: [ 'key' => 'method', 'operator' => 'in', 'value' => [ 'GET', 'HEAD' ] ].

The designer lays out the dialog the same way for every step. Settings named variable, onError, credential, operation and timeout get their usual places.

Running

  • $this->cfg($key, $default): a setting as saved. $this->expr($key, $default): with its {{ }} evaluated. A field that is only one expression keeps its type.
  • $this->exec->getVariable($name), setVariable($name, $value), log($this->wfid, $message).
  • execute() returns the output numbers to continue on ([ 0 ], [ 1 ]…), [] to finish without continuing, self::SLEEP to be called again later (Wait keeps its own state, e.g. $this->resume_at), or null to keep the token and wait (Merge waiting for its other inputs). A waiting step may implement release(): it is called when nothing else can arrive, and returns outputs to continue on, or null.
  • Throw an \ErrorException with a clear message to fail the step. Its message becomes the execution's error.
  • For On error support, add an onError select (Fail the step / Continue on the error output) and an $outPorts on it. Catch your errors, put them in the result variable, and return [ 1 ].

Credentials

A step that connects to a service takes a credential of the project. Add a credential select whose choices are the project's credentials of the needed kind, and look the credential up with \models\Credential::findFor($this->workflow, $id, '<capability>'). A credential kind is a class extending \models\Credential, registered as 'variant-of' => 'Credential', with its own fields. Fields marked encrypt are stored encrypted and never shown again.

Triggers

A trigger has $type = 'trigger' and $inputs = 0. To be startable with Run, implement startNow($wf, $node). For a schedule, set $scheduled = true and implement runScheduled($wf, $node, $at). Other triggers start executions with \models\WfExecution::startFor($wf, '<trigger>', $input, $nodeId) from their endpoint.

Testing

Add checks to the check suite (app/commands/CheckCommand.php, one suite…() per area) and run ./v check::run --only=<suite>.
